CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a certificate of recognition to Dr. Sandra E.
  Thomas, for her lifelong commitment to Pasadena, with over 40
  years of effective community service, commitment to teaching,
  developing and mentoring students, and dedication to the
  betterment of the City. Dr. Thomas thanked the Mayor and City

Council Minutes  1  07/17/2023

  Pasadena.

  Mayor Gordo and Coach Joe Blackman recognized Mia Reid of La
  Salle College Preparatory School upon placing 8th in the Girls 100
  Hurdles Varsity event at the 2023 GIF California State Track & Field
  Championship Finals, named San Gabriel Valley Girls Track and
  Field Athlete of the Year and earned a scholarship to compete for
  Cal State Fullerton. Coach Btackman and the Mayor also
  recognized Mia's parents, La Salle Track & Field teammates Alex
  Alvarez, Daniel Alvarez, and Olivia Bohanec, and other team
  parents.

  Mayor Gordo introduced the 3rd Annual Robert Gorski Access

  Disability Commission, to provide introductory comments on the

  thanked the City for the award and recognition.

  Councilmember Lyon thanked Acting Director Carmona for the
  comprehensive report: and the public speakers for their comments.
  He recognized that tonight's discussion has made it evident that this
  is a matter people genuinely care about. He emphasized the need
  to continue to empower residents through education and information
  on dealing with coyote interactions, and the need for continuing the
  conversation on the matter. Councilmember Lyon made a motion for
  staff to initiate Option 3, which includes the following recommended
  actions (outlined on page 8 of the agenda report):

  1. Increase public outreach services.
  2. Improve local coyote reporting systems.
  3. Convene a panel of coyote experts to improve our collective

D  understanding of effective approaches.
  4. Hire a consultant to conduct a field study where community
  concerns are heightened.
  5. Support residents to strengthen their properties against
  coyote intrusion.

  Councilmember Madison voiced his support for Option 3; he
  emphasized that the purpose of the conversation was to address all
  community concerns regarding the increase in sightings of coyotes
  and the potential risks to the safety of the community, and stated that
  he believes the overall conversation was beneficial for everyone. He
  suggested that the City's Public Health Department form a liaison
  with California Fish and Wildlife agency on this issue. Furthermore,
  he stated that the personal and political attacks by members of the
  PETA organization were unnecessary and uncalled for.

  Councilmember Hampton voiced his support for Option 3 and
  inquired about the impacts of neutering coyotes would have on their
  population.

  Manual Carmona, Acting Director of Public Health, stated he would

L  further seek additional information from CA Fish and Wildlife
  regarding the effects of neutering coyotes, as well as questions
  related to natural predators for coyote.

  Council Minutes  9  07/17/2023
   Vice Mayor Williams thanked the public speakers for their
  comments. She voiced her support for Option 3, and requested the
  maker of the motion amend the recommendation in a way that
r  specifically addresses the impacts in the Arroyo, utilizing the Arroyos
  and Foothills Conservancy (AFC) data and expertise to develop
  solutions that are tailored to the Arroyo within the AFC study area
  and neighboring residence.

  Councitmember Madison (as the seconder of the motion) stated he
  does not support Vice Mayor's request to amend the motion, as
  detailed above.

  Manual Carmona, Acting Director of Public Health, acknowledged
  Vice Mayor Williams comments and stated that staff would be
  utilizing geographical analysis to identify areas of concerns. As the
  City and staff gain further understanding of the local coyote
  population, he expects that hotspots will become evident in the
  community based on complaints and concerns, which will in turn
  require and gain attention.

  In response to Mayor Gordo comments on collaborating with the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments' (SGVCOG) Coyote
  Management Task Force and other local agencies on the issue of
  coyotes and public safety, it was agreed that staff would initiate
  discussions and work with other local agencies, stakeholders, and
  cities on the issue of coyotes and wildlife safety.

  It was moved by Councilmember Lyon, seconded by
  Councilmember Madison, to approve the staff recommendation and
  direct staff to implement Option No. 3 (incorporating the five
  recommendations on page 8 of the staff report, and as noted above),
  as well as direct City staff to initiate discussions and work with other
  local agencies, stakeholders, and cities on the issue of coyotes and
  wildlife safety. (Motion unanimously approved) (Absent: None)
